oneTimers: A $69M discrete tax benefit (about 5 cents of EPS) that was not in the company's original guidance — operating taxes were $166M, less $69M of discrete items, for a $97M provision.

The year-ago quarter included a $124M restructuring/other credit, largely a gain on asset sales, which did not repeat — that is most of why the Other segment's operating profit fell 55% to $78M even as its revenue grew 23%.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net of $80M, less $128M of interest and debt expense — a net $48M drag. The $97M tax provision is $166M of operating taxes less a $69M discrete tax benefit.
pngFooterNote: Revenue up 11% to $4.07B on broad demand recovery.

segments.name: Analog
segments.note: Analog chips — the workhorse of industrial and automotive electronics; up 13% YoY. Segment operating profit was $1,206M.

segments.name: Embedded Processing
segments.note: Microcontrollers and processors for connected devices; down 1% YoY. Segment operating profit was $40M.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Smaller product lines, including DLP and calculators; up 23% YoY. Segment operating profit was $78M.

takeaways.text: Revenue grew 11% to $4.07B and 2% sequentially, with every market growing sequentially except a seasonal decline in personal electronics. Analog, the biggest business, grew 13% to $3.21B; Other grew 23% and Embedded Processing slipped 1%.
takeaways.title: Sales grew in nearly every market

takeaways.text: Operating profit rose only 3% to $1.32B, a 32.5% operating margin, down from 35.1% a year ago. Gross margin narrowed to 56.8% and R&D plus SG&A together were $989M, up 6% while revenue grew 11%. Net income rose 7% to $1.18B and EPS rose 7% to $1.28, helped by a $69M discrete tax benefit.
takeaways.title: Profit grew slower than sales

takeaways.text: Free cash flow for the trailing 12 months was $1.72B, 10.7% of revenue, but just -$14M in the quarter itself after $1.12B of capital spending on new factories. TI still returned $1.89B to owners in the quarter — $1.24B in dividends and $653M in buybacks. Q2 guidance is $4.17–$4.53B of revenue and EPS of $1.21–$1.47.
takeaways.title: Cash is tight while factories get built

verdict: Texas Instruments earned $1.18 billion on $4.07 billion of revenue as sales grew 11% on a broad recovery, with operating profit up just 3% as margins narrowed.
